plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade the bid up or down. Bidding above value risks winning and overpaying relative to value; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $30, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $30, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay a fair second-price amount.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where the highest bidder wins but pays the second-highest bid. In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than the price I'd pay, and I never overpay. My value is $4, which is quite low, so I should bid conservatively at this true value to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is the dominant strategy. This is because I pay the second-highest bid regardless of my own bid (as long as I'm the highest), so bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $19, I should bid $19.
